hook.text: In 1890, two Boston lawyers wrote an article that invented the legal concept of privacy in America.

buildup.text: Samuel Warren was furious that newspapers published details of his wife's dinner parties.

discovery.text: Warren and Brandeis argued in the Harvard Law Review that people have a right to be left alone.

twist.text: The article had no legal force. But it inspired decades of court rulings and new privacy laws.

climax.text: One angry lawyer and one brilliant article gave America its first legal framework for privacy.

punchline.text: An angry dinner party sparked a legal revolution.

quiz.question: What motivated Warren and Brandeis to write about privacy?
options: Newspapers publishing details of private social events
A Supreme Court ruling they opposed
